title: Eagle Mom Slaps a Squirrel—and the Internet Can't Look Away!
summary: What happens when a flying squirrel sneaks into a bald eagle's nest in the middle of the night? A slap! Jackie, a famous bald eagle mom in California, was trying to sleep when Fiona the squirrel came too close. Jackie smacked her with a wing and made some noisy backtalk. The whole thing was caught on a 24/7 livestream watched by millions of fans. Jackie and her mate Shadow have two eaglets, Sandy and Luna, who hatched in April. The nest sits high in a pine tree overlooking Big Bear Lake. Flying squirrels like Fiona and Fast Freddie often visit at night, looking for leftover fish or eggshells. They're not dangerous to the chicks, but Jackie still doesn't want them around. The eaglets are getting big and practicing their wing flaps. Soon they'll fledge—that means leave the nest and fly for the first time. That's a risky time; only about 70% of young eagles survive. Dangers include cars when they scavenge for roadkill, bad weather, and other birds like ravens. Earlier this year, ravens destroyed Jackie and Shadow's first two eggs. But the pair laid new ones, and Sandy and Luna hatched healthy. The eagle family has had a roller coaster journey, with past chicks lost to snowstorms. But Jackie and Shadow keep trying, and millions of people cheer them on. Watching the livestream, you can see nature's drama up close—from squirrel slaps to first flights. It's a reminder that even in the wild, parents will do anything to protect their kids.
why_it_matters: This livestream lets you see how wild animals care for their babies, just like parents protect kids at home, and reminds us that nature is full of both tender and tough moments.

background_read: Jackie and Shadow are a real bald eagle pair whose nest in Big Bear Lake, California, has been watched online by millions of people since 2017, thanks to a live camera set up by a conservation group.
Bald eagles were once nearly wiped out in the U.S. because of a pesticide called DDT, but after it was banned they made a strong comeback and are now a conservation success story.
Flying squirrels are nocturnal and often visit nests to scavenge leftovers; they are harmless to chicks but mother eagles still chase them away.
Article_Structure: WHO: Jackie (a bald eagle mom), her mate Shadow, their eaglets Sandy and Luna, and the intruding flying squirrel Fiona.
WHAT: A squirrel snuck into the nest at night; Jackie slapped it with a wing, captured on a 24/7 livestream watched by fans.
WHERE: A nest high in a pine tree overlooking Big Bear Lake, California.
WHY: Jackie was protecting her chicks as they prepare to fledge; the livestream lets people witness the drama of nature and parenting.

perspectives.description: Loyal watchers get a unique chance to learn about eagle behavior and the challenges of raising young in the wild.
The slap is a natural reaction; eagles guard their nest against any creature, even harmless ones, because they can't take risks.
When Sandy and Luna fledge, it will be an exciting but dangerous moment, showing the real risks young eagles face in their first flight.
